book.title: Adult Children of Emotionally Immature Parents
book.author: Lindsay C. Gibson

confidence_note: Emotional loneliness without knowing why, life looking 'normal' because basic needs were met, three core problems (loneliness, disconnected relationships, low self-worth), childhood dream world, four parent types (emotional, driven, passive, rejecting) come from publisher/summary previews; book text not read. Old-text client dialogue and the 'glass wall' image were dropped as not tied to the book; the old claim that EIPs are 'mostly loving' also dropped.
facts: Gibson says adult children of emotionally immature parents often feel deeply emotionally isolated without knowing why.
The feeling is easy to dismiss because life can look normal or fine, especially when parents met basic needs such as shelter, food and clothing.
She names three core problems: deep loneliness, emotionally disconnected relationships and low self-worth.

One childhood coping strategy is creating a dream world to escape; the child imagines a better future, which helps endure, but carried into adulthood can lead to unrealistic expectations such as an effortless marriage.
Gibson describes four types of emotionally immature parent: emotional, driven, passive, rejecting.
A passive parent may be present and pleasant yet avoids anything upsetting.
scene_details: the dream world of a better future
tension: Everything visible was provided, yet the child felt alone.
opening_idea: Parents who met every basic need.

lessons.idea: Name what was missing even when basic needs were met.
lessons.anchor: Gibson: life looks fine because shelter, food and clothing were provided, yet loneliness remains.
lessons.everyday_example_idea: A person who says their childhood was fine but feels alone with close friends.

reflect_final: Where in your life do you feel alone even though nothing visible is missing, and what do you tell yourself about that?

use_cases.situation: A friend says their childhood was fine
use_cases.move: Ask what it was like to bring a worry home.

use_cases.situation: You feel alone with people around
use_cases.move: Write down what you wanted from them that did not come.

use_cases.situation: A sibling dismisses your feelings as ingratitude
use_cases.move: Say you are grateful for the care and also lonely.

pocket_idea: Food, a roof and clothes are care; feeling heard is a separate thing you can still miss.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: Life can look fine and still feel lonely.
